title: Who is earning a surplus?

predict.q: The wage stays at **12** and employment at **80** thousand; total earnings **960** thousand. The supply curve rotates from perfectly elastic to perfectly inelastic. What happens to economic rent?

options.s: It falls, because workers are less willing to change jobs
options.fb: Less willing to switch means fewer would leave if pay fell, so more of the pay is surplus: rent rises.

options.s: It rises, until all 960 is economic rent
options.fb: As S steepens, the area above S grows: 0, 160, 320, 480 and finally all 960 when S is vertical.

options.s: It stays the same, because total earnings do not change
options.fb: Total earnings stay at 960, but the split changes: the area under S shrinks as S steepens.

options.s: It falls to zero, while transfer earnings rise to 960
options.fb: That is the move towards perfectly elastic supply, the opposite direction.

task: Move the supply-steepness slider and watch the two shaded areas.

target.do: Move the supply-steepness slider all the way to "perfectly inelastic", then press Check.

takeaway: The same pay can be mostly surplus or mostly the cost of keeping workers; elasticity of supply decides.
